mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, thereby driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months in at least 5 out of the last 10 tightening episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) during episodes where GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters in at least 3 out of the last 5 such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) during periods when UNRATE exceeds 6% for two consecutive months in at least 4 out of the last 6 such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) during INDPRO declines lasting four consecutive months in at least 3 out of the last 5 such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous and significant decline in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) in the same month signals a broad-based collapse in demand, which depresses corporate earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both fall by >1% month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.7%) during months where both GDPC1 and HOUST decline by more than 1% month-over-month in at least 4 out of the last 6 such events.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is below 1% and the CPI inflation index (CPIAUCSL) rises above 2% for three consecutive months, it signals a low-rate, high-inflation regime where real yields turn negative, boosting equities via lower discount rates and higher earnings growth expectations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% AND CPIAUCSL > 2% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.8%) during periods when FEDFUNDS < 1% and CPIAUCSL > 2% for three consecutive months in at least 3 out of the last 5 such regimes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above the previous 12-month average for six consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month moving average for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.6%) during periods when PAYEMS exceeds its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months in at least 4 out of the last 6 such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) combined with a decline in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) in the same month signals a shift from spending to saving, which typically precedes a future rebound in consumption and earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS rises and GDPC1 falls in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1.0%) during months where RSAFS rises and GDPC1 falls simultaneously in at least 3 out of the last 5 such post-recession recovery periods.
